rule_a: If several ages tie for the highest frequency, return the smallest of those ages as the most common age.
rule_b: If several ages tie for the highest frequency, return whichever of those ages occurs first in the dataframe sorted by name and age in ascending order as the most common age.

class: Lists of dictionaries in which at least one of x, y, or z is present in some dictionaries but omitted from others.
rule_a: For each of x, y, and z that appears in at least one dictionary, calculate all five statistics using only dictionaries containing that key.
rule_b: For each of x, y, and z that appears in at least one dictionary, calculate all five statistics using every dictionary, treating an omitted key as zero.

class: Nonempty lists of dictionaries that contain additional keys alongside x, y, and z.
rule_a: If the dictionaries contain additional keys, return the scaled x, y, and z columns and retain the additional columns with their original values.

class: Lists of dictionaries containing explicitly stored None values under one or more of 'x', 'y', and 'z'.
rule_a: For each of 'x', 'y', and 'z', count explicitly stored None values as occurrences of None in that key's Counter.
rule_b: For each of 'x', 'y', and 'z', exclude explicitly stored None values from that key's Counter.

class: A nonempty list of letters repeated zero times, for which retaining or omitting zero-frequency letters is unspecified.
rule_a: If repetitions is zero, return a dictionary containing every distinct letter from the input list with frequency zero.
rule_b: If repetitions is zero, return an empty dictionary.

class: Alphabetic input strings containing uppercase English letters.
rule_a: Count adjacent two-letter occurrences after converting uppercase English letters to lowercase.
rule_b: Count adjacent two-letter occurrences without converting uppercase English letters to lowercase.

class: Text containing hyphenated compounds, whose treatment as whole words or separate component words is unspecified.
other_inputs: (pd.DataFrame({'text': ['This is a sample sentence.', 'Another example here.']}), 'text')
rule_a: Treat each hyphenated compound as a single word, preserve its internal hyphens, and remove it only if its lowercase form belongs to STOPWORDS.
rule_b: Split each hyphenated compound into component words, remove components whose lowercase forms belong to STOPWORDS, and join the surviving components with spaces.

class: Strings containing non-ASCII letters, for which the scope of “alphabetic characters” is unspecified.
rule_a: When sanitizing the input, retain all Unicode alphabetic characters recognized by str.isalpha(), preserving their case and order.
rule_b: When sanitizing the input, retain only ASCII alphabetic characters A–Z and a–z, preserving their case and order.

class: Single-character strings have no adjacent pairs, leaving the entropy of the empty difference array unspecified.
rule_a: For a single-character string, return an empty NumPy difference array and NaN as the entropy.
rule_b: For a single-character string, return an empty NumPy difference array and 0.0 as the entropy.

class: Inputs whose cleaned strings contain several two-letter combinations tied for the highest frequency.
rule_a: If several two-letter combinations share the highest frequency, return the lexicographically smallest combination and its frequency.
rule_b: If several two-letter combinations share the highest frequency, return the combination that first occurs in the cleaned string and its frequency.

class: Strings containing non-ASCII letters or digits, for which the scope of 'alphanumeric' is unspecified.
rule_a: Retain all Unicode letters and numeric characters, discard other characters, and lowercase the retained characters before counting.
rule_b: Retain only ASCII letters and digits, discard other characters, and lowercase the retained characters before counting.

class: Nonempty numeric DataFrames without NaN values whose row index differs from the default zero-based consecutive integer index.
rule_a: If the input has a nondefault row index, preserve that index in the output while keeping rows in their original order.
rule_b: If the input has a nondefault row index, replace it with a zero-based consecutive integer index in the output while keeping rows in their original order.

skip: For lowercase English words, the stated alphabet positions and examples determine the output; alternative handling of empty or non-English strings would rely on inputs outside the clearly defined domain.

class: Text containing non-ASCII letters or decimal digits, for which the scope of alphanumeric characters is unspecified.

rule_b: When cleaning text, retain only ASCII letters and digits, remove every other character, and count the retained characters.

class: Inputs containing only whitespace or no characters, so filtering leaves an empty DataFrame whose column dtype is unspecified.

rule_b: If filtering removes all lines, return an empty DataFrame whose single 'Text' column has object dtype.

class: Texts containing words with ASCII apostrophes between letters.
rule_a: Treat each word containing internal ASCII apostrophes as a single word, retaining the apostrophes in the returned word.
rule_b: Split each word containing internal ASCII apostrophes at those apostrophes, counting the resulting components as separate words.

class: Grade labels use both uppercase and lowercase letters, with no specified treatment of letter case when ranking categories.
rule_a: When grade labels use both uppercase and lowercase letters, convert them to uppercase and assign consecutive integer codes starting at zero to the distinct normalized labels in lexicographic order.
rule_b: When grade labels use both uppercase and lowercase letters, preserve their case and assign consecutive integer codes starting at zero to the distinct original labels in lexicographic order.

class: Inputs with repeated categories whose first-appearance order differs from their decreasing-frequency order.
rule_a: Insert category keys into the returned dictionary in decreasing order of their counts, breaking ties by first appearance in the input.
rule_b: Insert category keys into the returned dictionary in order of their first appearance in the input, regardless of their counts.

class: Texts containing contractions written with straight apostrophes.

rule_a: Treat each contraction containing a straight apostrophe as one whole word when matching stopwords.
rule_b: Treat each contraction containing a straight apostrophe as separate words split at the apostrophe when matching stopwords.

class: Lists in which two or more values associated with URL keys tie for the highest frequency.

rule_b: If several values tie for the highest frequency, return only the tied value encountered first while traversing the list and each dictionary in insertion order, together with its count.

class: Documents containing hyphenated compounds whose alphabetic components each contain at least two letters.

rule_b: For hyphenated compounds whose alphabetic components each contain at least two letters, calculate TF-IDF using each hyphen-separated component as an individual word.

class: Dictionaries whose word keys contain uppercase letters.
rule_a: When word keys contain uppercase letters, combine uppercase and lowercase forms of each letter into a single frequency under its lowercase key.
rule_b: When word keys contain uppercase letters, count uppercase and lowercase forms of each letter separately under keys preserving their case.
